import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Get the top N breeds to focus on
top_n = 12
top_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(top_n).index

# Filter the DataFrame to include only these top breeds
df_top_breeds = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_breeds)].copy()

# Ensure the breeds are ordered by overall count for consistent plotting
df_top_breeds['Rasse1Text'] = pd.Categorical(
    df_top_breeds['Rasse1Text'],
    categories=top_breeds,
    ordered=True
)

# --- Visualization ---
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8)) # Adjust figure size for better readability

# Create a countplot to show the distribution of top breeds by gender
sns.countplot(
    data=df_top_breeds,
    x='Rasse1Text',
    hue='SexHundLang',
    palette='viridis', # A colorblind-friendly palette
    order=top_breeds # Explicitly set order based on overall popularity
)

# Add titles and labels for clarity
plt.title(f'Distribution of Top {top_n} Dog Breeds in Zurich by Gender', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Dog Breed (Primary)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability, especially with longer breed names
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Add a legend
plt.legend(title='Dog Gender', loc='upper right', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
